themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 44 THIS WEEK, up 665% from the 5.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 15.08), suggesting a sudden, widespread deterioration in road infrastructure across Morningside Heights and Hamilton Heights.
evidence: 44 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (665% spike)
Z-score of 15.08 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Concurrent spike in street sweeping complaints (3 this week vs. 0.2 average, 1100% increase)
reporting_angles: What happened to neighborhood streets this week? Interview DOT, check for emergency closures or weather events.
Are potholes, flooding, or surface damage concentrated in specific blocks? Map complaints to find hotspots.

themes_detail.label: Street & Sidewalk Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from streets and sidewalks surged to 74 THIS WEEK, up 295% from the 18.8-complaint weekly average (z-score: 5.82), indicating a sharp increase in disruptive outdoor activity—construction, traffic, or street-level disturbances.
evidence: 74 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 18.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (295% spike)
Z-score of 5.82 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Overlaps with elevated street condition complaints, suggesting construction or infrastructure work
reporting_angles: Is the noise spike tied to DOT or construction work? Cross-reference with active DOB permits (276 filed in past 90 days, mostly alterations).
Talk to residents on heavily-complained blocks about noise source—construction, traffic patterns, street festivals?

themes_detail.label: Damaged Trees and Environmental Stress
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints hit 16 two weeks ago, a 6300% spike from the 0.2-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 36.37, highest severity), suggesting a weather event, disease outbreak, or infrastructure damage affecting the district's canopy.
evidence: 16 damaged tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (6300% spike, z-score: 36.37)
Highest z-score among all spikes, indicating extreme statistical anomaly
Timing suggests possible severe weather event or pest infestation
reporting_angles: Did a storm or high winds hit the neighborhood 2 weeks ago? Check weather records and parks department response.
Is this tied to a specific pest (emerald ash borer, spotted lanternfly) or disease? Interview Parks Department arborists.

themes_detail.label: Construction Lead Dust Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Construction lead dust complaints jumped to 4 last week, a 1500% spike from the 0.2-complaint weekly average (z-score: 8.66), signaling potential lead exposure risk in renovation projects across the district.
evidence: 4 construction lead dust complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike)
Z-score of 8.66 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Concurrent elevated alteration permits (245 filed in past 90 days) suggest extensive pre-1978 building renovation
reporting_angles: Which construction sites are generating lead dust complaints? Are contractors following EPA RRP (Renovation, Repair, Painting) rules?
Interview families with young children about health impacts; contact DOB and DOHMH about enforcement actions.

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles Accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints rose to 9 last week, up 260% from the 2.5-complaint weekly average (z-score: 7.51), suggesting a growing street-level blight and public safety concern in parking-strained neighborhoods.
evidence: 9 abandoned vehicle complaints last week vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (260% spike)
Z-score of 7.51 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Broader pattern: illegal parking complaints remain elevated (1,040 over 90 days), indicating systemic parking pressure
reporting_angles: Are abandoned vehicles concentrated in specific blocks? Map complaints and assess for chop shops or title recovery issues.
Interview NYPD or CTTB (City Tow Task Force) about removal timelines and resource constraints.
